business_model.claim: The company acquires, develops and operates airport concessions granted by governments, and says it operates 52 airports across Latin America, Europe and Eurasia.
quotes: We acquire, develop and operate airport concessions, positioning ourselves as a leading private airport operator in the world.
As of the date of this annual report, we operate 52 airports across Latin America, Europe, and Eurasia.

business_model.claim: Revenue is classified into four categories: aeronautical, commercial, construction service and other revenue.
quotes: We classify our revenue in the following categories: aeronautical revenue, commercial revenue, construction service revenue and other revenue.

business_model.claim: Aeronautical revenue, the largest category, was 934.7 (table in millions of U.S.$), or 47.6% of 2025 total revenue. It comes from the use of airport facilities by aircraft and passengers.
quotes: Aeronautical revenue is derived from the use of our airport facilities by aircrafts and passengers.

business_model.claim: Aeronautical fees are charged mainly to airlines, which either pay from their own revenue or collect the fees from their passengers.
quotes: These fees are invoiced to users of our airport infrastructure, principally airlines using our airports, either from their general revenue or as collected directly from airline passengers.

business_model.claim: Aeronautical tariffs are not set freely by the company. They are established or regulated by the concession agreements.
quotes: Our concession agreements establish or otherwise regulate the rates that we may charge to aircraft operators and passengers for aeronautical services.

business_model.claim: Commercial revenue was 813.1 (table in millions of U.S.$), or 41.4% of 2025 revenue. It comes from cargo warehousing, retail and duty free, parking, food and beverage, space rental, advertising, fuel, VIP lounges and similar fees.
quotes: The majority of our commercial revenue is derived from fees resulting from warehouse usage (which includes cargo storage, storage and warehouse services and related international cargo services), services and retail stores, duty free shops, car parking facilities, catering, hangar services, food and beverage services, retail stores, including royalties collected from retailers’ revenue, and rent of space, advertising, fuel, airport counters, VIP lounges and fees collected from other miscellaneous sources, such as telecommunications, car rentals and passenger services.

business_model.claim: Construction service revenue was 205.8 (table in millions of U.S.$), or 10.5% of 2025 revenue. It is booked under IFRIC 12 for concession-mandated improvements at cost plus a margin, against construction service costs of 193.5 (table in millions of U.S.$).
quotes: The amount of revenues for these services is equal to the amount of costs incurred plus a reasonable margin.
